subject: SLO fallback & traffic shaping plan + demo slotting (hosted vs incumbent)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morrison <alex.morrison@crescenthealth.com>, SRE <sre@crescenthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: SLO fallback & traffic shaping plan + demo slotting (hosted vs incumbent)

Thanks for the call today — quick recap + concrete next steps so everyone has the same picture. Appreciate the clear latency constraints and the openness on traffic patterns.

High-level outcomes we captured: 
- Target E2E SLOs you asked us to qualify (hosted API vs your incumbent): p95 <= 200 ms, p99 <= 450 ms (end-to-end from client -> your service -> model -> back to client).
- Baseline throughput: 80 rps sustained during normal hours, burst up to ~250 rps during peak windows.
- Streaming use case: 60 concurrent streaming sessions expected at baseline; up to 150 concurrent during black swan peaks. Each streaming session averages 1.2k tokens per request.
- Acceptable fallback behavior: if hosted capacity saturates, we should fall back to a quantized 8-bit variant (same model family) or an edge-optimized smaller model with explicit degradation notice. Confirmed that small, graceful quality vs latency trade is OK for short windows.

Immediate asks from our side: 
1) Please share the traffic CSV you mentioned (token distribution, request size, time-of-day breakdown) — uploaded a stub (crescent_traffic_profile.csv) for template completion.
2) Can SRE provide a 48-hour sample log export (time-synced traces) for one representative day so we can reproduce network + app latency in the lab?
3) Proposed demo window options: Jun 26 09:00–12:00 PT (preferred) or Jun 27 13:00–16:00 PT. We will run: a) synthetic ramp, b) replay from your logs, c) sustained soak at target throughput with streaming enabled.

Technical notes we will run ahead of the demo: 
- Prefix/KV caching enabled for repeated prompts (should reduce p95 by ~15–25% on cached workloads).
- Dynamic batching policy with QoS prioritization: short-latency requests get priority to avoid head-of-line blocking during bursts.
- Concurrency matrix: we will run quantized variant + standard FP16 variant to map latency/throughput tradeoffs and validate fallback thresholds.

Attachments: slo-proposal-draft.pdf (contains a draft acceptance table and rollback criteria).

Next steps: Alex — confirm which demo slot works and send the 48h log export. Procurement — if you want the MSA + work order templates in advance, we can share our standard redlines.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Cc: SRE <sre@crescenthealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@crescenthealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO fallback & traffic shaping plan + demo slotting (hosted vs incumbent)

Thanks Mina — appreciate the clear recap. Quick clarifications and confirmations: 

- The p95/p99 numbers are for full-stack E2E latency (client observable). Our service itself typically adds 30–80 ms depending on the request type; please account for that in your modeling.
- We will complete the csv by EOD Tue (token sizes + per-endpoint QPS). Attached a small sample log capture (sample-log-capture.json) to help with clock skew alignment.
- Demo: Jun 26 09:00–12:00 PT works for our SRE team. We request a 30-min warmup window before the public ramp so we can toggle feature flags on our side.
- Procurement: we can share the MSA, but we need a redline turnaround in 3 business days after we receive your standard MSA.

Two asks from our end: 
1) Can you confirm the exact behavioral difference we should expect when you fall back to the quantized 8-bit variant vs the smaller model (e.g., failure modes, quality delta, token-cost delta)? We want to communicate this to product.
2) Please include an estimate of expected token/compute cost for the demo run (ballpark is fine) so procurement has context.

Looking forward to the demo — Alex

--
Alex Morrison
Head of Platform Integrations, Crescent Health
alex.morrison@crescenthealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morrison <alex.morrison@crescenthealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, SRE <sre@crescenthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO fallback & traffic shaping plan + demo slotting (hosted vs incumbent)

Alex — thanks. A few concrete technical clarifications to set expectations for the Jun 26 run: 

1) Fallback behavior (quick bullets):
   - Quantized 8-bit variant: identical topology; we use int8 kernels and a slightly different cache footprint. Typical token-level quality delta is small for high-confidence prompts (<2% measured metric drift on our evals) but latency improves ~20% at high concurrency. This is our preferred first-line fallback.
   - Smaller model (edge-optimized): reduces computation more significantly; higher quality delta (we will show example regressions), but p95/p99 improves more aggressively. We will put an automatic annotation in the response metadata when we serve fallback tokens.

2) Demo traffic shaping plan (we will run from Redwood side unless you prefer to originate traffic):
   - 09:00–09:30: warmup (models loaded, caches populated).
   - 09:30–09:50: synthetic ramp from 10 rps -> 80 rps (15m ramp).
   - 09:50–10:30: replayed traffic from your logs at 80 rps sustained (streaming enabled).
   - 10:30–11:15: burst window: step up to 250 rps for 15m windows to observe tail behavior and fallback triggers.
   - 11:15–11:45: soak at 120 rps with mixed streaming/short requests to validate steady-state.

3) Concurrency & batching notes:
   - We will instrument dynamic batching and per-route QoS to prioritize short requests.
   - For streaming concurrency above ~100 simultaneous sessions we will gradually enable reduced chunk sizes + prefetch hints to keep p99 within the target band.

4) Cost estimate for the demo (ballpark):
   - Expected token volume (demo plan + replays): ~1.1M tokens.
   - Compute estimate: ~12 GPU-hours on dedicated inference pools (we will offset with shared queued capacity for the synthetic phases).
   - Estimated hosted bill for demo: ~$2.6k (this is an estimate to aid procurement). We will refine after we see your full traffic csv.

Link to the runbook and instrumentation checklist: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/demo-runbooks/CRESCENT-2028 (permission: redwood-demo-access).

Let us know if you want Redwood to originate the traffic (we can, but we'll need a short IP allowlist on your firewall and a feature-flag handshake).

-Ben
Ben Carter
Perf & Product Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Alex Morrison <alex.morrison@crescenthealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE <sre@crescenthealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO fallback & traffic shaping plan + demo slotting (hosted vs incumbent)

Thanks Ben — that level of detail is perfect. We will: 
- Complete the csv and upload to the drive by EOD today.
- Share the 48-hour trace as requested (SRE) and open a temporary allowlist for Redwood IPs for the run.
- Procurement will expect a short cost reconciliation after the demo; your ballpark is fine for now.

One final ask: during the burst window, if we see p99 drift above 450 ms even after fallback, would Redwood automatically shift traffic to a dedicated pool (if we have committed capacity) or gracefully shed with a 503+retry header? We need the operational behavior documented for our on-call runbook.

Appreciate the coordination. See you Jun 26 for the warmup.

-Alex
